title: Value of a linear Boolean function from its values on basis vectors
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a linear Boolean function, meaning $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, and for each coordinate $i$ let $e_i \in \{0,1\}^n$ denote the standard basis vector that is $1$ in position $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then for every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the value $f(x)$ equals the parity of the number of coordinates $i$ with $x_i = 1$ and $f(e_i) = 1$; that is, $f(x) = 1$ if that count is odd and $f(x) = 0$ if it is even.
hypotheses_covered: f is a linear Boolean function on the n-dimensional hypercube
x is an arbitrary point of the hypercube
replaced:
Specialization of the previous lemma to the support of an arbitrary point:
if $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ is linear, then for every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$
the value $f(x)$ is the parity of the number of coordinates $i$ with
$x_i = \texttt{true}$ and $f(e_i) = \texttt{true}$.
